title: Energy Crisis
description: Finland faces pressure to keep electricity affordable while maintaining a reliable, low-carbon energy system. Your government must weigh immediate relief against long-term investment and energy dependence.

analysis.summary: Provide temporary financial assistance to households facing high electricity bills.
benefits: Reduces the financial burden on households.
Provides immediate support during an energy crisis.
risks: Increases government expenditure.
Does not directly improve long-term energy independence.

outcome.summary: Temporary bill subsidies ease household pressure during the energy crisis. The immediate social benefit comes at a fiscal cost, while the country's energy supply remains structurally unchanged.

impacts.ECO: Funding electricity subsidies adds to public expenditure, reducing the government's available economic resources.
impacts.HAP: Lower electricity bills relieve pressure on family budgets and increase short-term public satisfaction.
impacts.ENV: Bill subsidies do not directly change electricity production or emissions in this game scenario.
impacts.SEC: The measure does not change Finland's dependence on energy suppliers or its security posture in this scenario.

analysis.summary: Invest in nuclear power to strengthen Finland's long-term electricity supply and reduce dependence on imported energy.
benefits: Supports low-carbon electricity production.
Strengthens long-term energy security and independence.
risks: Requires substantial upfront investment and long construction periods.
Does not provide immediate relief from high electricity prices.

outcome.summary: Investing in nuclear energy requires substantial resources now but supports a more reliable, low-carbon electricity system over time. The simulation rewards those long-term gains in environmental and energy security.

impacts.ECO: Planning and financing new nuclear capacity create an initial economic cost before the investment delivers returns.
impacts.HAP: A credible plan for future electricity supply gives households a modest confidence benefit, despite limited immediate relief.
impacts.ENV: Additional low-carbon generation can reduce reliance on higher-emission electricity sources over time.
impacts.SEC: More reliable domestic generation reduces exposure to imported energy and external supply disruptions.

analysis.summary: Seek to restore energy imports from Russia to reduce energy costs and support short-term economic activity.
benefits: Could reduce energy costs for households and businesses.
May provide short-term economic relief for energy-intensive industries.
risks: Increases dependence on a geopolitically risky energy supplier.
Could conflict with EU restrictions and weaken Finland's national security.

outcome.summary: In this hypothetical scenario, renewed Russian energy imports lower short-term costs for households and businesses. Those gains are offset by environmental pressure and greater geopolitical dependence; real-world imports face EU restrictions.

impacts.ECO: Cheaper imported energy reduces some operating costs, improving business activity in the simulated outcome.
impacts.HAP: Lower energy expenses provide short-term relief to households and improve perceived living conditions.
impacts.ENV: In the game model, renewed reliance on conventional imported energy slows progress towards cleaner supply.
impacts.SEC: Dependence on a geopolitically sensitive supplier increases vulnerability to political pressure and disruptions.

title: Education Crisis
description: Schools are under pressure to maintain educational quality and equal opportunities while public resources are limited. Your government must decide how education funding should be distributed.

analysis.summary: Allocate additional public funding to schools, teaching staff, and student support services.
benefits: May improve learning conditions and access to support for students.
Can reduce differences in educational opportunities between communities.
risks: Requires additional public spending when budgets are already constrained.
Higher funding alone does not guarantee better outcomes without effective implementation.

outcome.summary: More school funding improves access to teaching and student support. The social benefits are positive, but they require additional public resources.

impacts.ECO: Hiring staff and improving school services increase spending before longer-term educational returns can emerge.
impacts.HAP: Better learning conditions and more equitable support improve student and family wellbeing.
impacts.ENV: This education funding decision has no direct environmental effect in the game model.
impacts.SEC: The simulation does not assign an immediate national security change to this education measure.

analysis.summary: Link a larger share of school funding to measurable results and institutional performance.
benefits: Creates incentives to monitor outcomes and use limited resources efficiently.
May help identify effective teaching practices and successful programmes.
risks: Could disadvantage schools serving students who need more support.
May encourage a narrow focus on measured results rather than broader learning and wellbeing.

outcome.summary: Linking school funding to performance improves the model's measure of resource efficiency, but it can deepen inequality between schools and weaken public satisfaction.

impacts.ECO: More targeted spending and accountability improve the efficiency of limited public funds in this scenario.
impacts.HAP: Schools serving disadvantaged communities may lose resources, reducing perceived fairness and wellbeing.
impacts.ENV: No direct environmental effect is modelled from changing school funding criteria.
impacts.SEC: School performance funding does not directly alter Finland's security position in this round.

title: Forests at a Crossroads
description: Forests support Finland's jobs, exports, biodiversity, and climate goals. The country must decide how much priority to give to timber production versus protecting forest ecosystems.

analysis.summary: Allow increased timber harvesting to support the forest industry and economic activity.
benefits: Can create business activity and employment in forestry-dependent regions.
Provides more raw material for wood-processing industries and exports.
risks: Intensive harvesting can weaken forest carbon sinks and damage habitats.
Long-term ecosystem resilience and biodiversity may suffer if safeguards are insufficient.

outcome.summary: Expanded logging stimulates the forestry economy and supports some jobs. Increased harvesting, however, damages ecological outcomes and slightly weakens long-term resource resilience in the simulation.

impacts.ECO: Greater timber supply supports processing, exports, and related economic activity.
impacts.HAP: Employment and incomes in forestry-dependent communities provide a modest wellbeing benefit.
impacts.ENV: More intensive harvesting reduces habitat protection and can weaken forests' capacity to store carbon.
impacts.SEC: The game treats depletion of important domestic natural resources as a small loss of long-term national resilience.

analysis.summary: Strengthen forest conservation and limit harvesting in ecologically sensitive areas.
benefits: Protects habitats, biodiversity, and important forest ecosystems.
Can support carbon storage and the long-term resilience of natural resources.
risks: Restricts the supply of timber available to industry.
May reduce short-term income and employment opportunities in some forestry regions.

outcome.summary: Stronger forest protection preserves biodiversity and the long-term value of natural assets. Restrictions on harvesting reduce near-term industrial output, creating an economic trade-off.

impacts.ECO: Limits on timber harvesting restrict output and revenue for parts of the forest industry.
impacts.HAP: Protecting valued landscapes and ecosystems provides a modest public wellbeing benefit.
impacts.ENV: Conservation safeguards habitats, biodiversity, and forests' potential contribution to carbon storage.
impacts.SEC: Protecting strategic natural assets modestly strengthens resource resilience in the game model.

title: Healthcare Under Pressure
description: Healthcare services face rising demand, staffing pressures, and difficult budget decisions. Your government must find a way to sustain access to care without neglecting public finances.

analysis.summary: Reallocate public resources towards healthcare services and patient access.
benefits: Can help reduce pressure on care services and improve access for patients.
Signals a clear commitment to public health and social wellbeing.
risks: Increases pressure on the government budget or requires cuts elsewhere.
Shifting funds away from other services can create new problems in those sectors.

outcome.summary: Redirecting funding towards healthcare improves access to treatment and public wellbeing. The government pays for that improvement through added budget pressure or reduced spending elsewhere.

impacts.ECO: Moving more public resources into healthcare creates a short-term fiscal cost in this simulation.
impacts.HAP: Better access to services and less pressure on patients raise satisfaction and wellbeing.
impacts.ENV: Reallocating healthcare funding has no direct environmental effect in this scenario.
impacts.SEC: No direct national security effect is assigned to this healthcare funding choice.

analysis.summary: Raise additional tax revenue to strengthen the government's capacity to finance essential services.
benefits: Can improve the sustainability of public finances and future service funding.
May reduce the need for immediate borrowing to cover public spending.
risks: Higher taxes can reduce disposable income or increase costs for businesses.
The measure may be unpopular, particularly during a period of economic strain.

outcome.summary: Higher taxes improve the simulated public-finance position, providing a stronger basis for funding services. The burden on households and businesses nevertheless reduces public satisfaction.

impacts.ECO: Additional revenue strengthens the budget balance in the game's economic indicator, despite possible costs to private spending.
impacts.HAP: Households and businesses face higher tax burdens, reducing disposable income or perceived fairness.
impacts.ENV: This general tax increase has no separately modelled environmental effect.
impacts.SEC: The game does not assign an immediate security change to this tax policy.

title: The Future of Transport
description: Finland needs cleaner transport, but travel patterns differ greatly between cities and rural areas. Your government must choose where public investment can make the most difference.

analysis.summary: Expand public transport networks and service frequency, especially on high-demand routes.
benefits: Makes everyday travel more accessible for people without private cars.
Can reduce congestion and transport emissions when more people choose shared transit.
risks: Requires substantial investment and continued operating subsidies.
Low population density can make frequent services expensive outside urban areas.

outcome.summary: Expanding public transport improves mobility and offers cleaner travel alternatives. The benefits for residents and emissions require sizeable investment and ongoing operations.

impacts.ECO: Building and operating more transit services requires substantial public funding.
impacts.HAP: Better connections make commuting and essential journeys easier for more residents.
impacts.ENV: More viable alternatives to private car use can lower transport emissions and congestion.
impacts.SEC: Public transport expansion does not directly alter the national security indicator in this scenario.

analysis.summary: Support electric vehicle adoption and extend charging infrastructure into underserved rural areas.
benefits: Makes lower-emission driving more practical for people who depend on cars.
Improves charging access across the country rather than only in major cities.
risks: Public incentives and charging infrastructure still require funding.
Benefits may reach car owners first and do less for people who cannot afford a vehicle.

outcome.summary: Supporting electric vehicles and rural charging makes lower-emission driving more practical outside cities. The approach improves environmental outcomes but requires public investment and reaches people unevenly.

impacts.ECO: Charging infrastructure and vehicle incentives impose a public investment cost.
impacts.HAP: Residents who depend on cars gain charging options and somewhat greater travel convenience.
impacts.ENV: Replacing some combustion-engine journeys with electric travel reduces transport-related emissions in the model.
impacts.SEC: The simulation assigns no direct security change to rural charging expansion.

title: The Russian Relations Dilemma
description: Relations with Russia create a difficult trade-off between potential commercial opportunities and Finland's security commitments. Some proposed forms of cooperation may also conflict with current EU restrictions; this is a hypothetical policy scenario.

analysis.summary: Maintain a cautious relationship with Russia and prioritise security coordination with European partners.
benefits: Limits strategic dependence on a neighbouring state associated with major security risks.
Supports consistency with Finland's international commitments and security partnerships.
risks: Reduces opportunities for cross-border trade and some business sectors.
Adjustment costs may place pressure on firms and communities with historical trade links.

outcome.summary: Maintaining strategic distance from Russia sacrifices some commercial opportunities and produces short-term adjustment costs. It substantially strengthens Finland's security position within the game.

impacts.ECO: Reduced cross-border trade opportunities create costs for companies and affected regions.
impacts.HAP: Adjustment pressures and fewer economic opportunities modestly lower public satisfaction.
impacts.ENV: This diplomatic stance has no direct environmental effect in the simulation.
impacts.SEC: Reduced strategic dependence and closer alignment with security partners improve national resilience.

analysis.summary: Seek to restore extensive commercial relations with Russia, including activities that would require changes to existing EU restrictions.
benefits: Could reopen some markets and supply channels in a hypothetical easing of restrictions.
May offer short-term economic opportunities for businesses previously active in bilateral trade.
risks: Would face serious legal and diplomatic barriers under current EU sanctions.
Greater economic dependence could expose Finland to political pressure and security risks.

outcome.summary: In this hypothetical path, restoring extensive trade with Russia revives economic activity but sharply increases strategic dependence. Such restoration would require changes to applicable EU restrictions.

impacts.ECO: Reopened markets and supply channels stimulate commercial activity in the simulated scenario.
impacts.HAP: New trade opportunities and potential price relief improve short-term public satisfaction.
impacts.ENV: The model assigns a small environmental cost to renewed resource-intensive cross-border activity.
impacts.SEC: Closer economic dependence increases exposure to geopolitical coercion, diplomatic conflict, and supply disruption.

title: The Unemployment Crisis
description: Unemployment and weak household demand put pressure on public finances and social wellbeing. Your government must weigh incentives for businesses against direct support for families.

choices.text: Cut Corporate Taxes and Reduce Benefits

analysis.summary: Reduce corporate taxes to encourage business activity while lowering some unemployment benefits.
benefits: May improve incentives for investment and private-sector hiring.
Reduces some public transfer spending in the short term.
risks: Lower benefits can increase financial insecurity for unemployed households.
Business tax cuts may not generate jobs quickly if demand remains weak.

outcome.summary: Lower corporate taxes and reduced unemployment benefits improve the game's near-term business incentive and fiscal measures. The loss of household support creates social costs.

impacts.ECO: Tax incentives and lower transfer spending improve the model's short-term economic balance.
impacts.HAP: Reduced benefits make unemployment more financially difficult, lowering social wellbeing.
impacts.ENV: This labour-market and tax package has no direct environmental effect in the game.
impacts.SEC: No direct national security change is assigned to this employment policy.

analysis.summary: Strengthen household purchasing power through targeted support for people facing financial strain.
benefits: Helps families cover essential expenses and can improve social wellbeing.
May support local businesses by sustaining consumer demand.
risks: Requires additional government spending or financing.
Demand support alone may not address structural barriers to employment.

outcome.summary: Targeted household support reduces financial strain and sustains demand. The game scores its immediate budget cost more heavily than any short-term economic stimulus.

impacts.ECO: Additional support spending reduces the economic indicator despite possible benefits from consumer demand.
impacts.HAP: Families can better afford essentials, strengthening household security and overall wellbeing.
impacts.ENV: Direct household income support has no separately modelled environmental effect.
impacts.SEC: This policy does not directly affect defence or geopolitical security in the simulation.

title: Guns or Welfare
description: Finland must divide limited public resources between national defence and social welfare. Both priorities matter, but expanding one can constrain the other.

analysis.summary: Increase defence investment in equipment, preparedness, and military capabilities.
benefits: Can strengthen national readiness and deterrence.
Supports the ability to respond to changing regional security threats.
risks: Places substantial pressure on public finances.
May require postponing welfare improvements or other domestic spending.

outcome.summary: More defence investment significantly strengthens military preparedness and deterrence. The programme imposes a heavy budget cost and limits resources available for welfare priorities.

impacts.ECO: Procurement and readiness spending draw heavily on available public funds.
impacts.HAP: Fewer resources for domestic services and welfare reduce immediate public satisfaction.
impacts.ENV: The game assigns no direct environmental change to this defence spending decision.
impacts.SEC: Improved equipment, training, and readiness substantially raise national defence capability.

analysis.summary: Give greater priority to healthcare, social support, and other welfare services within the available budget.
benefits: Can improve daily wellbeing and support people facing hardship.
Reinforces access to essential public services.
risks: Leaves less fiscal room for defence upgrades and preparedness.
Security capabilities may develop more slowly as regional risks evolve.

outcome.summary: Prioritising welfare delivers immediate benefits to residents but leaves less room for defence investment. The government faces a fiscal cost while security readiness falls in the game.

impacts.ECO: Expanded welfare commitments consume public resources and weaken the short-term budget position.
impacts.HAP: Better access to healthcare and social support substantially improves everyday wellbeing.
impacts.ENV: No direct environmental change is modelled from the spending allocation.
impacts.SEC: Postponed defence upgrades reduce preparedness relative to the security needs assumed by the scenario.

title: The Public Debt Dilemma
description: Public debt and persistent budget pressure force the government to consider unpopular fiscal measures. Spending restraint and additional revenue both carry economic and social costs.

analysis.summary: Implement substantial cuts to selected government programmes to reduce expenditure.
benefits: Can improve the budget balance and limit additional borrowing.
May create more fiscal room for future priorities if savings are sustained.
risks: Cuts can reduce access to services and support that people rely on.
Lower public spending may weaken demand and cause hardship in affected communities.

outcome.summary: Major spending cuts improve the government's fiscal position in the simulation. Reduced services and financial support impose a particularly large social cost.

impacts.ECO: Lower expenditure improves the model's budget and debt outlook, even though real-world demand could also weaken.
impacts.HAP: Cuts to services and benefits create hardship and reduce public satisfaction.
impacts.ENV: The scenario does not assign a direct environmental change to these unspecified spending cuts.
impacts.SEC: No direct defence or geopolitical security effect is modelled for this fiscal decision.

analysis.summary: Increase taxes on consumption to raise government revenue without relying solely on spending cuts.
benefits: Can generate additional revenue to support public finances.
Allows some services to remain funded without equally deep direct cuts.
risks: Higher consumer prices reduce households' purchasing power.
Weaker consumption can weigh on businesses and affect lower-income households disproportionately.

outcome.summary: Higher consumption taxes raise revenue but make everyday purchases more expensive. The game models weaker demand and household purchasing power as the dominant short-term effects.

impacts.ECO: Higher consumer prices reduce spending and business demand enough to outweigh the modelled revenue benefit.
impacts.HAP: Households lose purchasing power, with a greater burden on those spending more of their income on essentials.
impacts.ENV: No distinct environmental change is assigned to this general consumption-tax increase.
impacts.SEC: The simulation assigns no direct national security effect to this tax choice.

title: The Green Industrial Transition
description: Finland wants stronger industrial competitiveness while meeting environmental commitments. Your final choice must balance new production and jobs against the ecological cost of industrial growth.

analysis.summary: Accelerate investment in strategically important industries and prioritise industrial expansion.
benefits: Can support employment, exports, and domestic production capacity.
Strengthens selected supply chains and economic resilience.
risks: Rapid expansion can increase emissions, energy demand, and pressure on land and resources.
Weaker environmental safeguards can create longer-term ecological costs.

outcome.summary: Accelerated investment in strategic industries strengthens jobs, production, and important supply chains. The gains come with a sizeable environmental cost from industrial expansion.

impacts.ECO: Investment and new industrial output increase production, employment, and export opportunities.
impacts.HAP: Job creation and stronger economic prospects support household confidence and wellbeing.
impacts.ENV: Faster industrial expansion increases pressure on energy, land, resources, and pollution controls.
impacts.SEC: More domestic capacity in strategic supply chains modestly strengthens economic and national resilience.

analysis.summary: Apply stronger environmental requirements to industrial activity and new investment.
benefits: Can reduce pollution and protect ecosystems over the long term.
Encourages cleaner technologies and more responsible production.
risks: Compliance and adaptation costs may slow some industrial projects.
Firms may postpone investments if requirements rise faster than their capacity to adjust.

outcome.summary: Stricter environmental standards protect ecosystems and encourage cleaner production. Compliance costs and slower projects reduce near-term economic activity, while wellbeing improves modestly.

impacts.ECO: Investment and compliance costs slow some industrial projects in the short term.
impacts.HAP: Cleaner environments and confidence in environmental protection improve public wellbeing.
impacts.ENV: Stronger safeguards reduce pollution and protect habitats and natural resources.
impacts.SEC: The scenario does not assign a direct security change to these environmental rules.
